newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares down 1.1 pct in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares down 1.1 pct in thin trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares fell in thin trade and continued profit-taking on Friday as the market entered a four-day holiday, but earlier losses were partially recouped on late selective buys, brokers said.
The stock market will be closed on Monday and Tuesday next week due to Republic day and reopen on Wednesday.

The IMKB-100 closed 925.12 points, or 1.11 percent lower at 82,420.98, but above an afternoon low of 81,367. Trade volume plunged to 12.84 trillion lira ($134 million) from yesterday's 16.12 trillion ($169 million).
Brokers said selective demand buoyed by nine-month profit outlooks earlier in the week faded as several firms released their results, some of which were below expectations.

Activity was subdued ahead of the four-day holiday and sentiment was also undermined by the European Parliament's decision to freeze millions of dollars of aid planned for Turkey as part of its customs union accord with the European Union.
Many brokers expect the index to remain within 81,000-84,000 range in the three trading days next week, with major resistance holding at 85,000.

The index had surged 29.3 percent from September 13 to Wednesday's all-time high close of 83,772.33, the tenth record in the medium-term uptrend. This week, it gained 0.83 percent after last week's 7.26 percent surge.
